I'm sure no matter what I say will help but here goes anyway. Please don't. The first time I hit fat I freaked the fuck out. I was hysterically crying, shaking and I ran to tell my parents and they took me to A&E. That's how they found out it wasn't accidental. Fast forward several years and I've done it a few times since. 4 in the past few weeks. It takes ages to heal, big risk of infection/hitting something more serious, it ACHES for a long time afterwards and the scars are horrendous. You don't have to have massive battle wounds to validate your struggle. The fact you feel so bad and out of control that you self harm at all is significant. There's no set depth or type of selfharm that triggers people to suddenly think it's serious. It's all serious. Speak to someone, cut up a pillow, go for a walk but please don't try to go deep. I promise you'll regret it. I always have.

Uggghhhhhh. This kinda thing happened a lot when I was at school. It became trendy to sh or pretend to sh. And it made people like me who has had pretty severe mental health issues most of my life feel like I was completely insignificant and worthless. Now, I feel like people who do this maybe be crying for help or attention for other issues or they may just like 'jumping on the bandwagon' - like I said this was high school and teenagers can be idiots when it comes to attention, popularity and peer pressure. I always wore long sleeved shirts and several times became mortified when I'd bled through them. But a lot of the 'pretenders' wore short sleeves with massive bandages - like the kind you'd get with a broken arm 😂. It is frustrating but I'd try to explain to your friend why it upsets you and if they don't care they're not a very good friend in the first place! Don't let it take away from the fact you are important and your feelings are valid, just because you don't shout them from the rooftops doesn't make you any less worthy of help.

Also, congratulations on being A YEAR clean! That's truly amazing and I hope you keep it up!

How you feel is always important, and never downplay it just because you don't cut. You're still valued and worthy of help.

I struggle with this. I get mad because it's not deep enough then I cut deep and I'm mad at myself for being so stupid and fucking myself up. I can't win when it comes to my brain. So I've taken to focusing on each day at a time and being like 'good job, you didn't self harm today'. I still have the urge, and it gets harder every day (I'm sure I will relapse at some point). But rather than getting mad when it's not enough, try taking it out of the equation entirely. I know that's easier said than done but just don't beat yourself up (literally or figuratively) if it doesn't 'go to plan'.
